What It Checks: Public HTTP LB should serve over HTTPS; an HTTP-only listener exposes all traffic in plaintext.
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: spec.https  OR  spec.https_auto_cert  (presence of either key)
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if either HTTPS key present (HTTPS listener). FAIL if neither (HTTP-only).
Remediation: Set listener type to HTTPS with Automatic Certificate (or custom cert) and enable HTTP→HTTPS redirect.

What It Checks: HTTP requests should redirect to HTTPS so no plaintext reaches the app.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if HTTP-only (see TLS-01). PASS if redirect true. FAIL otherwise.
Remediation: In the LB HTTPS settings enable "HTTP Redirect to HTTPS".

What It Checks: HSTS forces browsers to HTTPS-only, blocking downgrade attacks.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if HTTP-only. PASS if HSTS true. FAIL otherwise.
Remediation: In the LB HTTPS settings enable "Add HSTS Header".

What It Checks: TLS level should be Medium (TLS 1.2+) minimum; High preferred. Low permits TLS 1.0/1.1.
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: spec.https*/.tls_config | tls_parameters.tls_config | tls_cert_params.tls_config → low_security | medium_security | default_security, else min_version string
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if HTTP-only. FAIL if low_security or min TLS 1.0/1.1. PASS for medium_security, default_security, High.
Remediation: Set TLS Security Level to Default/High (TLS 1.2+). medium_security and low_security both permit TLS 1.0/1.1.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — BUG (confirmed, F5 TLS Reference Jun 2026): default_security = TLS 1.2/1.3; medium_security = min TLS 1.0; low_security = min TLS 1.0 + non-PFS static-RSA ciphers. Tool PASSes medium_security as "TLS 1.2+" → passes TLS 1.0/1.1. medium should WARN, low should FAIL; only default_security/High should PASS.

What It Checks: An App Firewall (WAF) policy should be attached. WAF is off by default.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if app_firewall ref present and not disabled. FAIL if disable_waf set, or no ref.
Remediation: Attach an App Firewall policy (Security Config → WAF → Enable).

What It Checks: Exclusion rules matching any domain + any path (or ".*") silence the WAF app-wide.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if 0 exclusions or all narrow. FAIL if any broad exclusion.
Remediation: Replace any "any domain / any path" (or ".*") exclusion with narrow per-signature, per-path exclusions.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — BUG: only reads legacy flat spec.waf_exclusion_rules[]. Misses newer spec.waf_exclusion.waf_exclusion_inline_rules.rules[] wrapper → broad exclusions in that shape are NOT detected.

What It Checks: Malware protection scans uploaded files. On by default unless disabled.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if not disabled. FAIL if disable_malware_protection present.
Remediation: Enable Malware Protection (licensed add-on) on LBs that accept file uploads.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — BUG (confirmed): Malware Protection is a licensed ADD-ON (GA Mar 2026), console default = Disable. "!disable_malware_protection" auto-PASSes every LB → over-credits. Entitlement should be Add-on (not Base); should verify genuine enablement, not just "not disabled". Consider scoping to upload-accepting apps.

What It Checks: A per-route override can disable WAF on specific paths. Sensitive routes must not bypass WAF.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if WAF not enabled at LB (see WAF-01). PASS if no route disables WAF. FAIL if ≥1 route does.
Remediation: Remove per-route "disable WAF" overrides, or confirm they are intentional on non-sensitive paths.

What It Checks: Path normalization defeats path encoding/evasion before security evaluation.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if HTTP-only. PASS if enabled. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Enable path normalization (route / more_option level).
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — BUG (confirmed): the top-level LB enable_path_normalize/disable_path_normalize oneof is DEPRECATED in the current schema; the active normalization setting lives under routes / more_option. Reading it off the HTTPS block never matches → always WARNs. Re-target to more_option/route, or retire this control.

What It Checks: A service policy controls L7 allow/deny. No policy = implicit allow.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if ≥1 active policy or inherits namespace policies. WARN if none.
Remediation: Apply an active service policy (or inherit the namespace set).
Known Issue / Review Note: Cannot see namespace-inherited policies unless the LB JSON names them — get_security_config would resolve effective policy.

What It Checks: IP Reputation blocks known-malicious source IPs (F5 threat intel). Must be explicitly enabled.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if enabled and not disabled. FAIL otherwise.
Remediation: Enable IP Reputation on the LB.

What It Checks: Threat Mesh shares cross-tenant threat intel. On by default unless disabled.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if not disabled. FAIL if disable_threat_mesh present.
Remediation: Enable Threat Mesh on the LB (it is OFF by default).
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — BUG (confirmed): F5 console default for Threat Mesh = DISABLE. Rule "!disable_threat_mesh" PASSes an LB that has NEITHER key (i.e. default-disabled) → false PASS. Should require enable_threat_mesh present (FAIL if disabled OR absent). Also category is WAF — consider ACCESS_CONTROL.

Control Name: No Broad WAF Bypass for Trusted Clients
What It Checks: A trusted-client rule that skips WAF for 0.0.0.0/0 effectively disables protection.
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: spec.trusted_clients[] → actions/skip_processing include *WAF*  AND  ip_prefix ∈ {0.0.0.0/0, ::/0, empty}
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if no broad WAF-skip rule. FAIL if a trusted-client rule skips WAF for all sources.
Remediation: Scope trusted-client WAF-skip rules to specific justified prefixes — never 0.0.0.0/0.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — now flags only ip_prefix 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 (an empty prefix, e.g. an ASN-scoped rule, is no longer false-flagged as broad).

What It Checks: CORS allowing any origin ("*") with credentials enables cross-origin data theft.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if no CORS policy. FAIL if wildcard origin AND allow_credentials. PASS if scoped.
Remediation: Restrict Allow-Origin to specific origins; never combine "*" with Allow-Credentials.

What It Checks: L7 DDoS auto-mitigation protects against application-layer floods.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if either configured. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Configure L7 DDoS auto-mitigation (l7_ddos_protection, default RPS threshold = 10,000) or DDoS mitigation rules.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — BUG: misses spec.enable_ddos_detection and spec.single_lb_app.enable_ddos_detection → can WARN even when DDoS detection is enabled via the app-profile path. Legacy l7_ddos_action_* is deprecated (current = l7_ddos_protection). Can cross-check coverage via get_security_config → ddos_detection[].

What It Checks: Request-header / request timeouts mitigate slow-loris connection-exhaustion attacks.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if either timeout set. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Tune slow DDoS mitigation timeouts if the defaults are unsuitable.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — Confirmed: when absent, system_default_timeouts apply (request_headers_timeout default = 10000 ms = Slowloris protection). "Not configured" ≠ unprotected → this should be INFO, not WARN.

What It Checks: An explicit max request body size limits buffer-abuse / large-payload DoS.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if > 0. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Set a max request size (buffer policy) appropriate to the app.

What It Checks: Bot Defense mitigates automated attacks (credential stuffing, scraping, carding). Licensed add-on.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if bot_defense object present and not disabled. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Attach a Bot Defense policy (requires Bot Defense Standard/Advanced license).

What It Checks: Behavioral analysis that scores users and mitigates high-risk ones.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if enabled. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Enable Malicious User Detection and configure a mitigation policy / user identifier.
Known Issue / Review Note: Checks DETECTION only. Does not verify a mitigation ACTION (challenge/block) is wired — detection without mitigation is half a control.

What It Checks: Rate limiting protects against brute-force and volumetric abuse. Metered add-on.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if any rate-limit construct present. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Configure a rate limiter with an appropriate user identifier.

What It Checks: CSD protects against Magecart / formjacking / skimming. Licensed add-on.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if CSD object present and not disabled. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Enable CSD on LBs serving payment / sensitive forms (requires license).
Known Issue / Review Note: Applied uniformly — most relevant for payment/PII apps; consider app-profile conditional grading.

What It Checks: API Discovery passively learns endpoints, surfacing shadow/zombie APIs.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if enabled. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Enable API Discovery and review the discovered inventory periodically.
Known Issue / Review Note: Discovery can also be enabled via spec.single_lb_app.enable_discovery / multi_lb_app (app_type) — not currently checked.

What It Checks: An attached API Definition (OpenAPI spec) enables positive-security schema validation.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if attached. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Upload an OpenAPI spec and attach it as an API Definition.
Known Issue / Review Note: Checks ATTACHMENT only, not ENFORCEMENT. Does not verify validation_all_spec_endpoints is in block mode or that fall_through_mode is not wide-open (a spec in report+fall-through enforces nothing).

What It Checks: Rate limiting & malicious-user detection rely on a user identifier. Client-IP-only misfires behind NAT.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if policy-based. WARN if client-IP-only or none.
Remediation: Attach a cookie/header-based user identification policy for authenticated apps.

What It Checks: Data Guard masks sensitive data (PAN, SSN) in responses.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if ≥1 rule. WARN if none.
Remediation: Configure Data Guard rules on pages/paths that may expose sensitive data.
Known Issue / Review Note: Distinct from sensitive-data DISCOVERY (spec.sensitive_data_disclosure_rules / default_sensitive_data_policy) which is not checked.

What It Checks: CSRF protection rejects cross-origin state-changing requests.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if enabled. FAIL if explicitly disabled. WARN if not configured.
Remediation: Enable CSRF protection and set allowed source-origin domains.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — csrf_policy.disabled is detected by key-presence (oneof empty object {}), not ===true, so an explicitly-disabled CSRF policy now FAILs correctly.

What It Checks: CSP / X-Frame-Options / X-Content-Type-Options / Referrer-Policy should be added on responses.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if ≥1 known security header added. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Add CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy on the LB.
Known Issue / Review Note: Also reads top-level spec.response_headers_to_add[] in addition to more_option.

What It Checks: Default response leaks a Server header (e.g. volt-adc). Remove/overwrite it.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if server header removed/overwritten. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Set the server-header option to overwrite/remove; avoid pass_through.
Known Issue / Review Note: Server-header handling is a more_option oneof: default_header (server="volt-adc", the default), pass_through (LEAKS origin software/version), server_name (overwrite), append_server_name. Should grade this oneof (pass_through = finding), not only response_headers_to_remove.

What It Checks: x-volterra-location (Add Location) discloses which XC PoP served the request.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: WARN if enabled (PoP disclosure). PASS if disabled.
Remediation: Leave "Add Location" disabled in production.

What It Checks: App cookies should carry Secure + HttpOnly via Protected Cookies.
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: spec.protected_cookies[] — each must have add_secure AND add_httponly
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: WARN if none configured. PASS if all hardened. WARN if some missing Secure/HttpOnly.
Remediation: Add Protected Cookies with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite for session cookies.

What It Checks: XC→origin traffic should use TLS for sensitive origins. Pools default to plaintext.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if TLS enabled. WARN if plaintext (no_tls / use_tls absent).
Remediation: Enable TLS to origin in the origin pool.
Known Issue / Review Note: WARN-level; for an HTTPS front-end terminating to a plaintext origin, consider FAIL where the app is sensitive.

What It Checks: When origin TLS is on, server cert verification must not be skipped (MITM risk).
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if no origin TLS. FAIL if skip_server_verification. PASS if verifying.
Remediation: Disable Skip Server Verification; use Volterra Trusted CA or upload the origin CA.

What It Checks: Production pool should have ≥2 origin servers across failure domains.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if ≥2 servers. WARN if <2 (no failover).
Remediation: Add a second origin server in a different AZ / failure domain.
Known Issue / Review Note: Availability/resilience control — arguably out of scope for a security audit; keep or move to a "reliability" section.

What It Checks: An active health check removes unhealthy origins from rotation.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if ≥1 health check. FAIL if 0.
Remediation: Attach an active HTTP/HTTPS health check with an expected response code.

What It Checks: Origin TLS should be TLS 1.2+ (Medium or higher), not a Low profile.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if no origin TLS. FAIL if Low. PASS for Medium/High/Default.
Remediation: Set the origin TLS security level to Default/High (TLS 1.2+).
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — Confirmed (TLS Reference): medium_security permits TLS 1.0 on the origin leg too — same fix as TLS-04 (medium should WARN, low FAIL).

What It Checks: Outlier detection ejects abnormal origins before hard failure.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if enabled. WARN if disabled or not configured.
Remediation: Enable outlier detection in origin pool advanced options.
Known Issue / Review Note: Resilience control, not strictly security.

What It Checks: A circuit breaker caps connections/requests to a failing origin.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if configured. WARN otherwise.
Remediation: Configure a circuit breaker (or enable the default) in advanced options.
Known Issue / Review Note: Resilience control, not strictly security.

Control Name: HTTP(S) Health Check with Expected Codes
What It Checks: App-layer (HTTP/HTTPS) health check with expected status codes detects real failures, unlike TCP-only.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: WARN if TCP-only. PASS if HTTP with expected codes. WARN if HTTP but no codes.
Expected Value: HTTP health check with expected status codes
Remediation: Use an HTTP/HTTPS health check with an expected status code and health path.

What It Checks: Custom TLS certs should have >30 days remaining; expiry = hard outage.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if expiry unknown (often auto-managed). FAIL if ≤7 days. WARN if ≤30 days. PASS if >30 days.
Remediation: Renew before expiry (cert + full chain) or migrate to XC auto-managed certs.
Known Issue / Review Note: Confirmed field: cert spec.infos[].expiry (RFC3339). Consider aligning thresholds to F5 built-in cert alerts: Expiring < 28 days (major), ExpiringSoon < 15 days (critical). Current 30d WARN / 7d FAIL is close but not matched.

What It Checks: Private key must be Blindfold/Vault-encrypted, never inline plaintext.
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: cert spec.private_key.{blindfold_secret_info | vault_secret_info | wingman_secret_info} vs clear_secret_info / "-----BEGIN"
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if blindfold/vault. FAIL if cleartext/PEM. SKIP if undeterminable.
Remediation: Re-import using a Blindfold-encrypted key or Vault reference.

What It Checks: Keys should be RSA ≥2048 or ECDSA. RSA-1024 is breakable.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if algorithm unknown. FAIL if weak (RSA<2048). PASS for RSA≥2048 / ECDSA.
Remediation: Reissue with an RSA ≥2048 or ECDSA P-256 key.

What It Checks: WAF must be in Blocking (or AI risk-based) mode in production; Monitoring only logs.
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: app_firewall spec.blocking | monitoring | ai_risk_based_blocking (oneof)  or  spec.mode string
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if blocking or ai_risk_based_blocking. FAIL if monitoring. WARN if undeterminable.
Remediation: Set the App Firewall enforcement mode to Blocking for production policies.

What It Checks: F5-curated threat-campaign signatures (e.g. Log4Shell) should be on. On by default.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if enabled (or detail present and not disabled). FAIL if disabled. SKIP if detection_settings unavailable.
Remediation: Enable Threat Campaigns in the App Firewall detection settings.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — GAP: a policy using default_detection_settings (F5 baseline — all attack types + high/med signatures + threat campaigns + all violations ON) has no detection_settings object, so this currently SKIPs. Treat default_detection_settings as PASS.

What It Checks: WAF should enforce the high & medium accuracy signature set (default).
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if a high/medium (or broader) set selected. FAIL if not. SKIP if detection_settings unavailable.
Remediation: Enable the high & medium accuracy signature set.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — GAP: default_detection_settings (baseline) enables high+medium signatures but has no detection_settings object → currently SKIPs; treat as PASS. Also only_high_accuracy_signatures currently FAILs (narrower than high+medium) — confirm desired grading.

What It Checks: WAF should block malicious bot signatures, complementing dedicated Bot Defense.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if malicious_bot_action = BLOCK. WARN if not blocking. SKIP if detail unavailable.
Remediation: Set WAF bot protection malicious-bot action to Block.

What It Checks: All OWASP attack-type signature categories should stay enabled.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if detection_settings unavailable. FAIL if ≥1 disabled. PASS if none disabled.
Remediation: Re-enable any disabled attack-type categories.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — GAP: default_detection_settings (baseline) enables all attack types but has no detection_settings object → currently SKIPs. Treat default_detection_settings as PASS (none disabled).

What It Checks: HTTP-compliance/evasion violations should stay enabled.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: SKIP if detection_settings unavailable. WARN if ≥1 disabled. PASS if none disabled.
Remediation: Re-enable any disabled violation types.
Known Issue / Review Note: ✅ FIXED — GAP: default_detection_settings (baseline) enables all violations but has no detection_settings object → currently SKIPs. Treat default_detection_settings as PASS.

What It Checks: WAF can enforce Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite on managed cookies.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if any cookie protection enabled. WARN if not. SKIP if detail unavailable.
Remediation: Enable cookie protection (Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite) in the App Firewall policy.
Known Issue / Review Note: Overlaps with LB-level COOKIE-01 (protected_cookies); both kept — confirm if intentional.

What It Checks: A terminal allow-all rule negates rules below it, disabling L7 access control.
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: service_policy spec.allow_all_requests, or rule (spec.rules[]/rule_list.rules[]) action ALLOW + any_client / any_ip (empty-object oneof)
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: FAIL if allow-all present. PASS otherwise.
Remediation: Remove/constrain any top-level ALLOW rule matching all clients.
Known Issue / Review Note: any_client detection was fixed to use key-presence (empty object), not ===true.

What It Checks: An ALLOW rule with 0.0.0.0/0 in its prefix list trusts every source.
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: FAIL if a broad allow-prefix found. PASS otherwise.
Remediation: Replace 0.0.0.0/0 in ALLOW rules with specific trusted prefixes.

What It Checks: A global log receiver streams security/access logs to an external SIEM.
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: count of shared/global_log_receivers objects (tenant-wide, run once)
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if ≥1 receiver. FAIL if 0.
Expected Value: At least one global log receiver
Remediation: Configure a Global Log Receiver (shared namespace) to your SIEM.
Known Issue / Review Note: Tenant-wide finding tagged to "(tenant-wide)" pseudo-LB; not per-app.

What It Checks: At least one alert policy + receiver should exist (errors, origin-down, cert-expiry).
XC Config Field(s) Inspected: count of alert_policys and alert_receivers (per scanned namespace)
How Evaluated (PASS / FAIL / WARN / SKIP: PASS if ≥1 policy AND ≥1 receiver. WARN if policies but no receivers, or none.
Expected Value: At least one alert policy + receiver
Remediation: Create alert policies and receivers for error rate, origin health, cert expiry.
